headline: One-time UK writedown swamps a solid underlying quarter
summary_short: Sun Communities posted a $992.7M GAAP net loss (vs. $1,273.6M income a year ago) after a $1.1B non-cash charge wrote its UK Park Holidays business down to fair value ahead of sale; Core FFO/share rose 4.5% to $1.84 and Same Property NOI grew 6.0% to $254.4M.
summary_long: The headline loss is a single non-cash item: Sun classified its UK Park Holidays business as held-for-sale/discontinued in Q2 2026 ahead of a sale expected to close in H2 2026 (pending UK FCA approval) and took a $1.1B valuation-allowance charge to mark it to the negotiated sale price, driving diluted EPS to -$8.08 from $10.02 a year ago. Continuing-operations Total Revenues were $484.6M, down 2.3% y/y per the filing's restated comparative (the shard's y/y comparator still reflects a pre-divestiture, UK-inclusive baseline). Same Property NOI rose 6.0% on 4.9% MH rent growth and 97.8% occupancy; Core FFO/share rose 4.5% to $1.84. Sun bought back $111.1M of stock and declared a $1.12/share dividend. No numeric forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: GAAP results were dominated by a one-time non-cash UK divestiture writedown; core U.S. manufactured-housing and RV operations grew NOI and Core FFO at a healthy clip.

Loss driven by a $1.1 billion non-cash valuation-allowance charge to write the UK Park Holidays business down to estimated fair value less costs to sell upon its Q2 2026 reclassification to held-for-sale/discontinued operations.
EPS moved in step with the net loss from the UK valuation-allowance charge, with a slightly higher diluted share count (127.0M vs 126.4M a year ago).

The shard's q/q and y/y comparators still include the now-divested UK business; the filing's own restated comparative shows Total Revenues down only 2.3% y/y ($484.6M vs $495.9M) on a continuing-operations basis.

The swing from a $73.2M pre-other-items loss to $50.2M income y/y reflects a smaller asset-impairment charge ($17.9M vs $33.4M) and no repeat of the $102.4M debt-extinguishment loss tied to the 2025 settlement of $3.2 billion in debt.
Growth driven by 4.9% MH and 3.2% RV average base-rent increases and higher MH occupancy (97.8% vs 97.4%), partly offset by higher supplies-and-repairs costs.
Not separately explained beyond the underlying Same Property NOI growth; the filing does not break out per-share Core FFO drivers further.
